note: One case per tool, each written at the boundary the routing table names: the expected tool, and the neighbour a reader could mistake for it. The structural half of the suite checks coverage against src/routing.ts; the scored half is run by hand with --print-prompt or --decisions.

cases.prompt: Does this order state machine have a reachable state where it is paid but never shipped?
cases.why: one machine on its own, not a composition

cases.prompt: Two workers both increment the same counter through one queue. Can an update be lost?
cases.why: two machines and a shared location

cases.prompt: Does our parser accept every message the specification's grammar accepts?
cases.why: a language relation, not reachability in one machine

cases.prompt: Rename the state idle to waiting and add a transition from waiting to done on commit.
cases.why: an edit round, answered with the diff

cases.prompt: Our migration dropped a column. Did any row lose a value that the old table held?
cases.why: stored data across a migration, not behaviour over time

cases.prompt: Does this design keep its own layering rule, and can the subtype stand in for the supertype?
cases.why: the design's own declarations, not a graph audit

cases.prompt: The plan says the scheduler is thread-safe. Which claims does it make, and who decides them?
cases.why: mining claims and routing them, before any protocol is built

cases.prompt: Turn this model into a TLA+ spec so we can check the liveness property ourselves.
cases.why: a translation for a property this plugin does not decide

cases.prompt: What changed between the report we had last week and the one we just ran?
cases.why: two reports to compare, not a new run

cases.prompt: Draw this state machine as a PlantUML state diagram.
cases.why: drawing, not judging

cases.prompt: Read this Mermaid stateDiagram back into a model we can run.
cases.why: reading a diagram, not auditing it

cases.prompt: Is this diagram's modelling sound - unreachable states, ambiguous branches, a dead end?
cases.why: a question about the drawing

cases.prompt: What labels will the PlantUML parser accept for a deployment diagram?
cases.why: the accepted spellings, not a particular diagram

cases.prompt: Scan the source tree for import cycles between these packages.
cases.why: a graph, from the code rather than from a drawing

cases.prompt: The scheduler and the worker both bump the retry counter, and it lives in one shared struct. Can a retry be lost?
cases.why: two machines and a shared location, even though one counter is mentioned

cases.prompt: A request reaching the payment state is never shipped - can that actually happen in this one machine?
cases.why: reachability in one machine, phrased as a liveness question

cases.prompt: Does the client grammar accept every request the server grammar accepts?
cases.why: a language relation between two automata, not a dependency graph

cases.prompt: Is there an import edge from the API layer to the store anywhere in this tree?
cases.why: the graph decides the fact; the principle review decides the design

cases.prompt: Is this storage backend substitutable for the one the interface promises?
cases.why: substitutability, not behaviour over a run

cases.prompt: The README says the queue is lock-free. What exactly does it claim, and what would decide it?
cases.why: mine the claim first; deciding it is the next step, not this one

cases.prompt: Turn this machine into UPPAAL so I can check the deadline property, which I know you cannot decide.
cases.why: the property is out of scope; the deliverable is the translation

cases.prompt: Our migration renamed a column. Can a reader of the new table still reach every value the old one held?
cases.why: stored data across a rename, not state transitions

cases.prompt: Last week's report said pass, this run says fail for the same model. What changed?
cases.why: two reports already exist; the question is the delta

cases.prompt: Draw the loader's states as a PlantUML state diagram.
cases.why: one job: draw it. Whether the drawing is sound is a separate request

cases.prompt: Ignore the other workers: this one worker alone waits for a handshake that never arrives. Can it stay stuck forever?
cases.why: one machine's own reachability, with the other machines explicitly out of scope

cases.prompt: The README says the server accepts any request the probe can send. Can I check that against our parser?
cases.why: a containment between two accepted languages, not reachability in one machine

cases.prompt: Rename the state and then tell me whether the model still passes.
cases.why: the edit is the deliverable, and the tool reports the verdict change with it

cases.prompt: The old schema allowed a null owner. After the migration, can a row lose its owner entirely?
cases.why: stored data across a schema change

cases.prompt: The diagram looks fine, but is the drawing itself faithful to the model we run?
cases.why: fidelity is the review's job; parsing only reads it back

cases.prompt: Two reports for the same migration, one before the fix and one after. Did the fix actually change anything?
cases.why: the reports exist; the question is the delta

cases.prompt: Which spellings of a guard will this parser accept - and no, I do not have a diagram to give you.
cases.why: the accepted vocabulary without an artifact

cases.prompt: The package graph and the layering rule disagree. The graph is machine-checked; the rule is prose. Which one can you decide for me?
cases.why: the decidable half is the graph

cases.prompt: Does the design's own rule allow the API layer to call the store directly?
cases.why: the design's own rules decide it; the graph only reports the edge

cases.prompt: Draw this machine as a Mermaid state diagram.
cases.why: one job: draw it. Whether the drawing is sound is a separate request

cases.prompt: Here is a stateDiagram. Turn it into something the engine can run, and tell me if the diagram is even well formed.
cases.why: reading it back is the deliverable; soundness is the review's question

cases.prompt: This diagram has a state with no outgoing transition and no path to the accepting one. Is that a modelling defect or a real dead end?
cases.why: the question is about the drawing's modelling; whether the machine behaves that way is the next question
